cards.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad (James 1:1). He just finished warning them that the tongue is a fire no man can tame (James 3:6-8). Now he throws out a new question: "Who is wise and understanding among you?"

cards.question: James asks who's wise and understanding among them. How does he say that person should show it?

answers.text: By good conduct done in humility

cards.text: Wisdom you can SEE. But James knows what else can hide in a heart: bitter jealousy and selfish ambition. If that's in there, he says, don't boast in it and don't deny the truth.

cards.question: How does James describe the kind of wisdom that comes with bitter jealousy and selfish ambition?

cards.text: Not from above. Earthly, unspiritual, demonic. Three words, and he went from earthly to DEMONIC in two steps. Friend, that ESCALATED.

cards.question: James warns that wherever jealousy and selfish ambition exist, ___ and every evil practice will be there too.

cards.text: Then James flips to the other side: the wisdom from above. And he doesn't stop at one word. He brings a whole LIST.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT on James's list for the wisdom from above?
James says the wisdom from above plays favorites.

cards.text: Here's the list: "first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere." That's the exact opposite of the group chat right after somebody posts their promotion.

cards.question: James wraps up this thought with a farming picture. What do peacemakers who sow in peace reap?

cards.text: Then James gets personal. He looks right at their conflicts and quarrels and asks where they come from.

cards.question: James says their conflicts and quarrels come from the passions at war within them.

cards.text: They crave what they don't have, they kill and covet and still can't get it, and they quarrel and fight. Reminds me of the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, fighting for YEARS over who had the most charge left when NOBODY had any.

cards.question: James says one reason they don't have what they want is simple: they don't ___.
Some of them DO ask, and they still don't receive. Why, according to James?

answers.text: They give up asking too soon

cards.text: They want it so they can squander it on their pleasures. That's asking your boss for a raise and having it all spent before the meeting's even over.
Then James gets LOUD: "You adulteresses!" No warm-up, no small talk, friend. He just kicked the door open.

cards.question: James asks if they know what friendship with the world is toward God. What does he call it?

cards.text: So whoever chooses to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God. That's showing up to the big game in BOTH teams' jerseys, and nobody in that stadium is buying it.
Then James asks a hard question: "Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?"

cards.question: Right after that hard question about the Spirit and envy, James says God gives us more grace.
James backs it up with Scripture: God opposes one kind of person and gives grace to another. Who gets the grace?

cards.text: "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble." So, James says, submit yourselves to God.

cards.question: James tells them to resist the devil. What does he say the devil will do?
James tells them to draw near to God. Then he says what God will do: God will ___.

cards.text: James keeps going: "Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded." Double-minded? That's our friend in both jerseys again.

cards.question: James tells them it's time to turn their mourning into laughter.

cards.text: Other way around: "Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom." No punchline here, friend. James means it.

cards.question: James says if they humble themselves before the Lord, He will exalt them.

cards.text: After all that talk about the tongue, James comes back to how they speak about each other. Brothers, he says, do not slander one another.

cards.question: James says whoever speaks against his brother or judges him is really speaking against the ___.

cards.text: And if you judge the law, James says, you're not a practitioner of the law but a judge of it. That's the baker at the cookie contest who grabs the clipboard and starts handing out ribbons.

cards.question: James says there is only one Lawgiver and Judge. How does he describe that One?

answers.text: The one able to save and destroy

cards.text: Then James drops it, nice and quiet: "But who are you to judge your neighbor?" Friend, I'm a cookie stamper. I press dough. Nobody ever handed me a gavel.
